disclosures.text: A handsaw comprising a handle and a blade releaseably mountable on the handle.
The handle comprises a lock assembly.
The handle comprises a stabilizing clamp assembly.
The blade comprises a lock engaging region located toward one end thereof.
The lock assembly includes a lock structure and an engageable actuator.
The lock structure is movable between a lock position and a release position.
The lock structure lockingly engages the lock engaging region of the blade in the lock position.
The lock structure is released from engagement with the lock engaging region in the release position.
The actuator is actuatable to move the lock structure from the lock position to the release position.
The stabilizing clamp assembly moves between a clamp position and a release position.
The clamp assembly applies a clamping force to side surfaces of the blade in the clamp position.
The clamp assembly releases the clamping force in the release position.
The lock assembly includes a spring biased lock structure.
The lock structure is biased towards the lock position.
Translational movement of the blade into engagement with the lock structure moves the lock structure against the spring bias.
The lock structure locks with the lock engaging region of the blade after moving against the spring bias.
The handle has a slot and internal guide surfaces.
The guide surfaces guide the lock engaging region of the blade into locking engagement with the lock structure.
The guiding occurs when the blade is moved translationally into the slot.
A saw blade comprising a cutting edge with a plurality of cutting teeth.
The saw blade comprises a locking engaging region constructed and arranged to be locked to a handle.
The lock engaging region comprises a plurality of cam surfaces disposed in spaced relation to one another.
The spaced cam surfaces include an upper cam surface and a lower cam surface.
Each cam surface engages a lock element of a lock structure.
Each cam surface comprises a recess disposed forwardly thereof.
The cam surfaces and recesses are shaped and positioned to enable translational movement of the lock elements toward the blade.
The cam surfaces and recesses enable forced engagement with the cam surfaces.
The lock elements ride along the cam surfaces during continued movement.
The lock elements ride over the cam surfaces and into the recesses.
A saw blade comprising a cutting edge having teeth.
The saw blade comprises a lock engagement region disposed at a proximal end portion of the blade.
The lock engagement region is opposite a distal end portion of the blade.
The lock engaging region comprises an upper lock structure and a lower lock structure.
The upper lock structure and the lower lock structure each comprise an opening leading to a recess.
As the recess extends away from the opening, it extends at an angle that extends away from the teeth.
The recess angle extends towards the distal end portion of the blade.
At least one of the lock structures comprises a curved cam surface.
As the curved cam surface extends towards the recess, it extends in a direction towards the teeth.
The curved cam surface extends towards the distal end portion.

A saw blade comprising a cutting edge with teeth and a lock engagement region at a proximal end; the lock engaging region having upper and lower lock structures, each with an opening leading to a recess that angles away from the teeth and t
The lock engaging region comprises a pair of recesses.
The lock structure comprises a pair of pins.
The pins engage with the recesses on the blade to lock the blade to the handle.
The lock structure comprises a spring.
The spring biases the lock structure toward the lock position.
The lock assembly moves linearly to disengage the pins from the recesses.
The handle comprises a first portion and a second portion joined to each other.
The joined portions define a slot therebetween.
The slot receives the blade therein.
The clamp assembly comprises an eccentric cam rotatable about a pivot axis.
The stabilizing clamp assembly includes a connecting member connected to the eccentric cam.
The connecting member passes through an opening in the blade.
The connecting member engages with a securing member.
The securing member engages with the second portion of the handle.
The first portion includes a notch therein.
The notch receives a portion of the stabilizing clamp assembly.
The notch receives the clamp member and the connecting member.
The stabilizing clamp assembly further comprises a spring.
The spring applies or enhances the clamping force to the side surfaces of the blade.
Movement of the clamp assembly from release to clamp position rotates the eccentric cam.
The rotated eccentric cam causes a portion of the stabilizing clamp assembly to bear against the blade side surfaces.
The bearing action applies clamping force to the blade.
The blade includes an alignment mark located on the blade.
The alignment mark provides an indication whether the handle is accurately positioned on the blade.
The lock structure is linearly movable between the lock and release positions.
The spring returns the lock structure to the lock position.
Linear translational movement of the blade into engagement with the lock structure moves it against the spring bias.
